children: Alstom signed contracts with TransPennine Express valued at around 1.2 billion euros ($1.39 billion) for the supply and long-term maintenance of a fleet of battery-electric trains, the French train maker said Friday.

The agreements include a rolling stock contract valued at about 930 million euros for 29 five-car battery-electric multiple units, with maintenance contracts valued at roughly 230 million euros, Alstom said.

The trains will be used for rail travel in northern England as part of the Transpennine Route Upgrade. The company will deliver the fleet from 2032, which will support decarbonization of the rail corridor, Alstom said.
The order will be booked in the second quarter of Alstom's 2027 fiscal year.
